segments.t: At the agency office in Paris, Mathias's wife Catherine arrives unexpectedly, hoping to travel down to Cannes to surprise her husband. Desperate to book a ticket when all flights are sold out, Catherine turns to Noemie, unaware that the assistant must sacrifice her own secret ticket. Listen to the scene in French first.
Bonjour, Noémie, vous partez?
Vous rejoignez Mathias à Cannes?
Je veux lui faire la surprise!
J'ai besoin de son programme.
Vous pourriez me réserver un vol?
Mais tout est complet aujourd'hui.
Les choses vont beaucoup mieux entre nous.
Je vais imprimer le programme de Mathias.
Tous les vols sont complets, madame.
Et pour le train?
Une place reste dans le train de nuit.
Je peux lui apporter des croissants!
Tu es mon sauveur, Noémie!
Merci pour votre aide précieuse.
Mathias ne peut pas se passer de toi.
Let's walk through the conversation step by step.
Bonjour, Noémie, vous partez?
'Hello, Noemie, are you leaving?' Catherine starts with polite 'you,' turning 'you leave' into a question simply by raising her voice at the end.
Vous rejoignez Mathias à Cannes?
'Are you joining Mathias in Cannes?' Built from 'join' with 're-,' this action means catching up with someone who has already traveled ahead—without needing any preposition before 'Mathias.'
Je veux lui faire la surprise!
'I want to surprise him!' Literally 'make the surprise to him,' French builds 'surprise someone' around 'make' rather than a single action word.
J'ai besoin de son programme.
'I need his schedule.' Literally 'I have need of his program,' where 'program' is the everyday French term for an event itinerary or schedule.
Vous pourriez me réserver un vol?
'Could you book a flight for me?' Notice 'for me' tucked right before 'reserve' as 'me,' and 'a flight' coming from the word that means 'fly.'
Mais tout est complet aujourd'hui.
'But everything is fully booked today.' False friend alert: for hotels, trains, and planes in French, 'complete' means 'sold out' or 'fully booked'!
Les choses vont beaucoup mieux entre nous.
'Things are going much better between us.' Just like English, French uses 'things go' for how life or a marriage is going, boosted by 'a lot better.'
Je vais imprimer le programme de Mathias.
'I will print Mathias's schedule.' Near-future 'I go print' sounds natural in French, and 'schedule of Mathias' avoids English apostrophe-s.
Tous les vols sont complets, madame.
'All flights are fully booked, madam.' Because 'flights' is plural here, 'complete' picks up a plural '-s' in spelling even though it sounds identical aloud in French.
Et pour le train?
'What about the train?' Opening with 'and for' is a super-handy phrase in French whenever you want to pivot and ask 'what about...?'
Une place reste dans le train de nuit.
'One seat remains on the night train.' Literally 'train of night,' joining the travel style with 'of,' while 'place' means an available seat or berth.
Je peux lui apporter des croissants!
'I can bring him croissants!' For carrying objects like pastries rather than people, French chooses 'bring' built on 'carry' rather than 'lead.'
Tu es mon sauveur, Noémie!
'You are my savior, Noemie!' Notice Catherine suddenly switching from polite 'you' to warm casual 'you' out of sheer relief—then switching right back in the next breath!
Merci pour votre aide précieuse.
'Thank you for your valuable help.' Literally 'help precious,' returning to formal 'your' as Catherine collects herself.
Mathias ne peut pas se passer de toi.

'Mathias cannot manage without you.' Literally 'pass himself of you,' that idiomatic expression is how French says 'do without someone.' Now let's listen to the whole scene again at normal speed, and see how much more you catch.
Bonjour, Noémie, vous partez?
Vous rejoignez Mathias à Cannes?
Je veux lui faire la surprise!
J'ai besoin de son programme.
Vous pourriez me réserver un vol?
Mais tout est complet aujourd'hui.
Les choses vont beaucoup mieux entre nous.
Je vais imprimer le programme de Mathias.
Tous les vols sont complets, madame.
Et pour le train?
Une place reste dans le train de nuit.
Je peux lui apporter des croissants!
Tu es mon sauveur, Noémie!
Merci pour votre aide précieuse.
Mathias ne peut pas se passer de toi.
Heartbroken and conflicted, Noemie gives up her own overnight train ticket so that Mathias's wife can surprise him in Cannes. See you next time!
À demain!
